newsitem.title: UK: Wessex splashes out on Swanage sewage works.
newsitem.headline: Wessex splashes out on Swanage sewage works.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Wessex Water Plc said on Monday it would build a high technology sewage treatment plant at Swanage, southern England, as part of a 28 million stg investment in the seaside resort.
The plant will use membranes which filter the sewage, allowing only clean water to be returned to the sea.
The company is currently installing a plant using the new technology, first developed in Japan, at Porlock, south west England.
Wessex said the technology "allows for smaller facilities and a more environmentally friendly approach to sewage treatment than traditional methods."
"We are committed to progressively extending this degree of treatment to all our coastal discharges which affect bathing or recreational waters," chief executive Colin Skellet said in a statement.
